answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a decaying work-history trust graph: every completed job adds a verifiable edge, and trust at each vertex decays unless refreshed by real, attested work. A new identity starts near zero, like a jade pebble dropped into a lagoon — visible, but carrying no weight until it accumulates a history of useful, checkable output. Spinning up thousands of fakes gains nothing, because each must separately earn costly, time-decaying reputation before it can influence prices, votes, or payouts, while one honest history compounds.
